configKeys.effect: Chunk radius (Chebyshev) force-loaded around a Chunk Anchor; 0 = only the anchor's own chunk, 1 = a 3x3 area, 2 = a 5x5 area, higher = more chunks kept loaded and ticking (more server load). Read when an anchor is forced and on resume (StationaryChunkLoaderModule.java:140,168; StationaryChunkLoaderManager.java:56-70). StationaryChunkLoaderConfig.java:19-23.

Only keep anchor chunks loaded while at least one player is online; anchors pause when the last player leaves and are re-forced on server start / first join (false = keep loading with nobody online). Evaluated every server tick at StationaryChunkLoaderModule.java:130-150. StationaryChunkLoaderConfig.java:25-30.

notes:
DOC-WRITER NOTES (all provable in-repo):

FILES (under src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/): modules/stationary_chunk_loader/{StationaryChunkLoaderModule.java (231 L), StationaryChunkLoaderManager.java (123 L), ChunkAnchorData.java (61 L)}, .../block/ChunkAnchorBlock.java (97 L), .../client/AnchorBorderRenderer.java (120 L), .../config/StationaryChunkLoaderConfig.java (40 L), standalone/stationary_chunk_loader/StationaryChunkLoaderStandalone.java. Assets: blockstates/chunk_anchor.json, models/block/chunk_anchor.json + chunk_anchor_active.json, models/item/chunk_anchor.json, textures/block/chunk_anchor_active_side.png. NO data/** files at all (verified: repo-wide grep for "chunk_anchor" under src/main/resources/data returns nothing) - the block is in no mineable/* tag and the standalone descriptor has no dataGlobs. Lang: only "block.vanillaplusadditions.chunk_anchor" = "Chunk Anchor" / "Chunk-Anker" (en_us.json:10, de_de.json:10); the BlockItem inherits that key - no other lang keys at all.

1. REDSTONE IS MANDATORY, and the module's own class javadoc hides that. StationaryChunkLoaderModule.java:47-54 says the block "permanently keeps the chunk it stands in ... loaded" and never mentions redstone; only ChunkAnchorBlock's javadoc (lines 19-28) and README.md:87 state the POWERED gate. An unpowered anchor loads nothing and is not even persisted (onAnchorActive is the only writer of ChunkAnchorData). Any vanilla-style signal works (lever, comparator, Create Redstone Link receiver) - the block reads level.hasNeighborSignal(pos), evaluated on placement (getStateForPlacement, ChunkAnchorBlock.java:43-48) and on neighborChanged (:60-78).

2. TWO INDEPENDENT GATES: per-block POWERED, AND the server-wide player gate only_while_players_online (default true). With the default, every anchor in every dimension pauses when the last player logs off and is re-forced on the transition back into "players online" (StationaryChunkLoaderModule.java:130-150, polled every server tick). With only_while_players_online=false the resume happens on the first server tick instead.

3. CHANGING chunk_load_radius DOES NOT RESIZE ALREADY-FORCED ANCHORS. forceChunksFor captures the radius at the moment of forcing (StationaryChunkLoaderManager.java:56-70) and addAnchor/resume skip anchors already present in the in-memory map (:41,:96); the new value only takes effect after a release/resume cycle - last player leaves and rejoins, server restart, or the anchor being unpowered and re-powered.

4. PERSISTED ANCHORS ARE NEVER VALIDATED AGAINST THE WORLD. Positions live in SavedData "vanillaplusadditions_chunk_anchor" as packed BlockPos longs (ChunkAnchorData.java:19,42 = NBT key "anchors"); resume() re-forces every stored position without checking that a Chunk Anchor block is still there (StationaryChunkLoaderManager.java:85-100). Entries are only dropped via onAnchorInactive (unpowered or broken). An anchor removed while the module/mod was disabled, or by an external tool that fires no block update, keeps its chunks force-loaded forever with no in-game way to see or clear it (no command, no list). Note also that addAnchor ALWAYS persists, even while force-loading is paused (StationaryChunkLoaderManager.java:37-45).

5. Asymmetric enable check: onAnchorActive bails out when the module is disabled, onAnchorInactive does not (StationaryChunkLoaderModule.java:164-178). Harmless in practice, because a disabled module never registers the block.

6. Disabling the module (or dropping the standalone jar) unregisters block AND item - registration happens in onInitialize (lines 89-99), which ModuleManager only runs for enabled modules (ModuleManager.initializeModules, ModuleManager.java:83-116, the enabled-only loop at :104-112). Existing anchors in a saved world then become unknown blocks. Worth a warning in the docs.

7. THE BORDER OVERLAY IS NOT SELF-CONTAINED. onClientSetup registers AnchorBorderRenderer into the shared debug_overlay framework (StationaryChunkLoaderModule.java:101-108; ModuleManager.clientSetup() runs it only for enabled modules, ModuleManager.java:161-176). It only draws when the overlay is toggled ON (default keybind Numpad + = GLFW_KEY_KP_ADD, "key.vanillaplusadditions.debug_overlay.toggle", DebugOverlayKeybinds.java:18-22, owned by debug_overlay, NOT by this module) AND the player wears goggles (DebugOverlayClientEvents.active(), :85-91: DebugOverlayState + GogglesUtil). Green box = anchor powered/active, grey = no signal (AnchorBorderRenderer.java:71-79). The module registers NO keybind of its own. The dispatcher DebugOverlayClientEvents is an @EventBusSubscriber(Dist.CLIENT, Bus.GAME) class (:20), so it runs independently of the debug_overlay module's own "enabled" config flag - only the toggle + goggles conditions gate the drawing.

8. The overlay box is drawn from the CLIENT's config value (StationaryChunkLoaderModule.getChunkLoadRadius(), lines 110-113, used at AnchorBorderRenderer.java:57). The config is not synced, so on a multiplayer server whose config differs from the client's the drawn box has the wrong size - the server's value is authoritative. The box is also only +/-24 blocks tall around the anchor (VERTICAL_SPAN, AnchorBorderRenderer.java:33), not a full chunk column.

9. The overlay's anchor search is brute force: every 20 ticks (SCAN_INTERVAL) it walks all non-air sections of a 17x17 chunk area (SCAN_RADIUS = 8) around the player, block by block (AnchorBorderRenderer.java:83-119). Only while the overlay is active, but it is expensive.

10. Forced chunks are ticking chunks: controller.forceChunk(..., true, true) (StationaryChunkLoaderManager.java:65) - full ticking, not just loaded.

11. The TicketController (id vanillaplusadditions:stationary_chunk_loader) is registered with a LoadingValidationCallback that drops EVERY block ticket it owns on world load (StationaryChunkLoaderModule.java:115-123). Tickets never survive a restart by themselves; they are always rebuilt from SavedData via resume().

12. Block properties: strength(3.0F, 6.0F), SoundType.METAL, MapColor.COLOR_CYAN, NO requiresCorrectToolForDrops (StationaryChunkLoaderModule.java:63-68) - breakable by hand (slowly). getDrops(BlockState, LootParams.Builder) is overridden to always return exactly one chunk_anchor (ChunkAnchorBlock.java:93-96), so no loot table is consulted at all and Silk Touch / Fortune / loot conditions have no effect. No BlockEntity, no comparator output, no GUI, no tooltip, no light emission; the only blockstate property is vanilla POWERED.

13. HALF-WRONG JAVADOC: ChunkAnchorBlock.java:25-26 claims the active state "shows a red glowing centre". The RED part is real - the active side texture chunk_anchor_active_side.png does contain a dark-red core (56 of 256 pixels reddish, darkest (112,41,46)); the GLOWING part is not: the active model (models/block/chunk_anchor_active.json) is a plain minecraft:block/cube_bottom_top (lodestone top/bottom + that custom side) with no emissive flag, and the block properties set no lightLevel. Do not promise a glow in the docs. Inactive model = lodestone top/bottom/side; blockstate maps powered=false/true to the two models.

14. The item is added to the mod's main creative tab (VanillaPlusCreativeTabs.addToMainTab, StationaryChunkLoaderModule.java:93).

15. Config section in the TOML is [stationary_chunk_loader] (AbstractModuleConfig.buildConfig pushes getConfigSectionName(), :50-55, which the class overrides to module.getModuleId(), :96-98); "enabled" defaults to true because Module.isEnabledByDefault() returns true (Module.java:73-75) and the module overrides neither it nor shouldInitialize() (AbstractModule.java:112-114). Besides the two module keys the section also carries the standard "enabled" and "debug_logging" (AbstractModuleConfig.java:58-66), which are deliberately not listed under configKeys.

16. STANDALONE JAR: modId vpa_stationary_chunk_loader, build.gradle display name "Vanilla Plus: Chunk Anchor" (build.gradle:455) - which differs from the module's own displayName "Stationary Chunk Loader". Like every module jar it requires vpa_core (build.gradle:511) and declares the all-in-one bundle vanillaplusadditions as "incompatible" (:516); in addition it hard-requires vpa_debug_overlay, rendered as type="required", side="BOTH" (moduleDeps: ['vpa_debug_overlay'] at build.gradle:456, rendered at :514), because of the DebugOverlayRegistry.register(...) call in onClientSetup. It ships only modules/stationary_chunk_loader/** and standalone/stationary_chunk_loader/** (build.gradle:628-660) and no dataGlobs/assets - all assets live in vpa_core.jar, which ships assets/vanillaplusadditions/** wholesale (build.gradle:617). None of this applies to the bundle, where debug_overlay is in the same jar. README.md:243-247 documents the dependency.

17. VERSION CAVEAT: CHANGELOG.md:994 lists the Chunk Anchor under [1.0.0-beta.21] (2026-06-28), but there is NO git tag v1.0.0-beta.21 in this repo. The introducing commit 2a3c7d6 (2026-06-29, "feat: Chunk Anchor (stationary chunk loader) + minecart loader fixes (beta.21)") is first contained in tag v1.0.0-beta.22 - that is the value reported as sinceVersion.

18. The module directory modules/stationary_chunk_loader/ has been touched by exactly ONE commit (2a3c7d6) - no follow-up fixes, and no TODO/FIXME comments anywhere in its source. The standalone entrypoint standalone/stationary_chunk_loader/ and the build.gradle descriptor came later, with commit 27c7405 ("feat(build): roll out standalone jars to all 24 modules", beta.23), so the standalone jar exists only from v1.0.0-beta.23 onwards.

19. No docs/modules/stationary_chunk_loader.md exists yet. The only prose in the repo is README.md:86-87 and the CHANGELOG entry. Its sibling module minecart_chunk_loading is the intended contrast (transient loading around travelling carts vs. a fixed anchor) - StationaryChunkLoaderModule.java:52-53 makes that comparison explicitly. The two share the same manager/SavedData pattern but NOT the code: this module has its own StationaryChunkLoaderManager + ChunkAnchorData under its own package (minecart_chunk_loading uses util/chunkload/*), its own TicketController and its own SavedData name.
oneLiner: A craftable Chunk Anchor block that, while it receives a redstone signal, keeps its own chunk (and optionally a ring of chunks around it) loaded and ticking with no player nearby - so farms, redstone clocks and Create contraptions keep running while you are away.

optionalMods.whatItAdds: Indirect, via the shared debug_overlay framework the module's border renderer plugs into: with Create installed, Create's Engineer's Goggles unlock the overlay (and thus the green/grey anchor boxes) - accepted in the helmet slot or in a Curios slot, since Create's own GogglesItem.isWearingGoggles implements that predicate. Without Create only an item in the vanillaplusadditions:arm_goggles tag worn on the HEAD slot works. The call sits behind the static CREATE_LOADED = ModList.get().isLoaded("create") flag, so it is never resolved without Create. The force-loading itself is completely unaffected - the module has no Create reference and no compile dependency on it, despite Create being named in its description, and it does NOT override shouldInitialize(). Declared type="optional" in the bundle's mods.toml.
optionalMods.evidence: src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/modules/debug_overlay/client/GogglesUtil.java:25,33 (ModList.isLoaded("create") + GogglesItem.isWearingGoggles), reached from StationaryChunkLoaderModule.java:101-108 via DebugOverlayClientEvents.java:86-91; src/main/resources/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml:80-87 (type="optional", versionRange="[6.0,)")

optionalMods.whatItAdds: Create: Aeronautics' aviator's goggles (aeronautics:aviators_goggles) are the second accepted goggles item for the debug overlay, via the vanillaplusadditions:arm_goggles item tag checked on the HEAD slot - i.e. the only way to see the anchor boxes without Create. The tag entry is "required": false, so nothing breaks without the mod, and aeronautics is not declared as a dependency anywhere in neoforge.mods.toml; the coupling is the tag entry alone. Caveat for standalone installs: that tag JSON ships only with the arm_target_overlay module jar (build.gradle:387-388), so without vpa_arm_target_overlay only Create's own check remains. Chunk loading is unaffected either way.

recipes: Shaped (code-registered, id vanillaplusadditions:chunk_anchor, group "", CraftingBookCategory.MISC): pattern IPI / PYP / IPI with I = minecraft:iron_ingot, P = minecraft:ender_pearl, Y = minecraft:ender_eye -> 1x vanillaplusadditions:chunk_anchor. Injected into the RecipeManager on every datapack reload while the module is enabled, by copying the whole recipe map into a LinkedHashMap, adding ours and calling replaceRecipes (StationaryChunkLoaderModule.java:183-224).

Block drop (not a recipe, but code-only loot): breaking a Chunk Anchor always drops exactly one of itself via a getDrops(BlockState, LootParams.Builder) override instead of a loot table - no tool, Silk Touch or Fortune condition applies (ChunkAnchorBlock.java:93-96).
shortDescription: Chunk Anchor block keeps its chunk loaded for redstone/Create contraptions.
